correctness.rationale: Nonzero digit positions convert lunar factorization exactly to Minkowski sums. The integer critical-pair inequality and equality case reduce every composite five-point support to (2,3) factors. The three possible overlaps of a three-point set with its translate give two explicit support families; their parameter counts have precisely the 3- and 4-divisibility exclusions. The only family intersection is the five-term arithmetic progression. Independent integer-set enumeration verified the counts for all degrees 4 through 130 and all factor-size shapes through 14, without using numerical enumeration to prove the universal statement.

Unindexed priority risk is retained.

value.rationale: The exact number of primes at prescribed binary digit weight is a natural refinement of the 2003 lunar-prime counting problem and of the 2025 density-one theorem. Weight five has a mathematically distinguished combinatorial boundary: two structurally different sumset families with an exceptional progression overlap. Their full classification produces a period-twelve exact count and sharp order m^(-2) for exceptions in this constrained stratum, neither an arbitrary chosen finite slice nor a known-table recomputation.
